subject: Follow-up: token economics & transient throughput exception (post-demo)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@nimbleretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:04:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: token economics & transient throughput exception (post-demo)

Thanks for taking the demo today, Sarah — really appreciated the clarity on the integration pattern. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can nail the pricing and temporary throughput guardrails.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: product search + conversational assistant on web + promotional push notifications.
- Baseline steady-state: ~1.5M tokens/day (inferred from sample qps you shared).
- Peak events: marketing promos could drive short bursts — you estimated ~4–6M tokens in a 1–2 hour window during promotions.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to budget ~$800–$1,000 per 1M tokens (target $/1M tokens ~ $850).
- Monthly budget range: rough band $40k–$65k.

Open questions for NimbleRetail (so we can propose a precise allowance + overage):
1) For "burst" behavior, is the 4–6M tokens in 1–2 hours an absolute cap, or do you expect multiple such bursts per month?
2) Do you need hard rate guarantees (hard cap) or soft limits with queued/dropped requests acceptable during extreme events?
3) Any regulatory/log retention requirements we should lock into the Private plan vs Hosted?

Preliminary Redwood proposal (to discuss internally and with you):
- Baseline quota: set at 1.5M tokens/day (30-day rolling).
- Transient throughput exception: allow up to 3x baseline for short windows (configurable windows; e.g., 2–6 hours) with automated throttling beyond that to protect latency SLOs.
- Overage pricing for burst consumption beyond allowance: $1,200 per 1M tokens (discounted volume pricing for sustained over-usage).
- Optional 30–90 day trial period with an elevated burst allowance (2–3x baseline) and a capped overage ceiling to limit spend surprises.

Next steps I propose:
- Sarah: confirm whether NimbleRetail prefers a hard cap or a soft/queued approach for promo bursts.
- We (Redwood): run a short internal pricing check and propose 2 options — a conservative allowance (tight caps + lower overage) and a flexible allowance (higher burst with higher overage).
- Share a mutual action plan + estimated numbers for legal/finance review.

I attached the sample traffic CSV you mentioned (I pulled the example you uploaded) and a short SLA-request form so we can see the items legal will ask for.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0123

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@nimbleretail.com>

Cc: NimbleRetail SRE <sre@nimbleretail.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics & transient throughput exception (post-demo)

Thanks Markus — great summary and thanks for pulling that CSV. A few answers inline: 

1) Bursts: We expect typically 1–2 large promotional bursts per month; during big seasonal promotions (e.g., flash sales) it could be 2–3 in a month. Bursts are usually 1–3 hours.
2) Preference: soft limits work for us if you surface throttling clearly and provide an SLA for queued request latency. We cannot have silent dropped requests during checkout flows — those need hard protection and fallback to a secondary flow.
3) Retention: standard e-commerce data retention, nothing special for PII — we will need audit logs for access.

Budget: The $40k–$65k monthly band is still our target. The $850/1M token target is ideal but we understand some premium for transient allowances.

I've attached the traffic extract and the SLA doc that our procurement team will use to scope questions.

Can you outline two explicit pricing scenarios:
- Scenario A (conservative): baseline quota + tight burst window (2x for 2 hours), overage price, and a hard cap for checkout flows.
- Scenario B (flexible): broader transient allowance (3x for up to 6 hours), higher overage, and a monitor-and-alert workflow with sticky rate-limits per route.

If you can get these to us by Monday EOD, procurement will start an initial review.

— Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Head of Product Operations, NimbleRetail
sarah.bennett@nimbleretail.com

Attachments: nimble_traffic_report_apr.csv, SLA-request.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 17:08:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Follow-up: token economics & transient throughput exception (post-demo)

Quick internal notes on pricing guardrails and what engineering can support without infra changes: 

Engineering constraints / suggestions:
- We can support route-level soft throttles and per-API-key burst windows out of the box.
- Hard protection for checkout flows: recommend a dedicated route pinned to a lower-latency tier with a small dedicated capacity pool. That prevents drops during promo peaks.
- Default burst policy: 2x baseline sustained for up to 4 hours; above that triggers autoscale + throttling rules. If they need 3x for longer than 6 hours we should discuss reserved capacity (Dedicated).

Pricing suggestions (to keep within Nimble's budget band):
- Scenario A (conservative): baseline 1.5M tokens/day. Burst allowance: +2x for up to 2 hours. Overage: $1,050 per 1M tokens. Hard cap option for checkout route at no additional cost (requires route pinning in account config).
- Scenario B (flexible): baseline 1.5M tokens/day. Burst allowance: +3x for up to 6 hours (one free promo burst per month). Overage: $1,400 per 1M tokens; monthly spend cap option to limit surprises.

Action items for sales thread:
- Markus: propose Scenario A and Scenario B to Sarah with clear example math for a 30-day month and a single promo burst.
- Ben: prepare a short readout on Dedicated pricing if they want consistent headroom for multiple bursts.
- Karthik: can you confirm the feasibility of issuing a soft burst allowance that automatically converts to a reserved capacity recommendation if sustained > 72 hours?

— Marissa
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
